statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk stays low because the overnight range still contains price after a completed round trip, while stress is high across the energy, rates and yen channels.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC covering the post-holiday US cash reopen. Tail remains well below the block threshold; the elevated readings sit in stress rather than in a persistent no-retracement price path.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its overnight range as oil, rate-hike talk and a six-month-high yen lift stress into the US reopen
body: NQ futures trade near 29,560, essentially unchanged on the session, and the day's range is still 29,478.00 to 29,764.75: the overnight advance was fully retraced earlier and the past hour added no extension in either direction. That intact retracement mechanism, with VIX near 15.8, is the central reason tail risk stays low, because mean reversion is visibly still working rather than failing. Stress is a different matter and has broadened. WTI trades near $94 and Brent near $99, the highest since early summer, after verified Houthi strikes on Saudi energy facilities that wounded more than 70 people and halted operations at several sites, including the Jizan refinery. A second channel has become more prominent: the yen reached a six-month high near 152.89 as revised Japanese GDP and the strongest wage growth since 1997 left a 25 basis point Bank of Japan move on 17-18 September close to fully priced, which is forcing carry-trade unwinding. The rates channel remains live with the 2-year near 4.34% and the 10-year near 4.77%, and rising energy costs have revived talk of a Federal Reserve hike after August payrolls added 162,000. Cross-asset signals conflict rather than align: Nasdaq-100 futures are flat while Dow futures are down about 0.8%, S&P futures about 0.3% and Russell futures about 0.3%. US cash equities reopen at 13:30 UTC after the Labor Day holiday, which is the flagged window; that reopen is treated as a checkpoint, not as observed one-way structure.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed in the EA_ON band with tail between 5 and 10 and no reading near the block threshold. Stress climbed from the mid-50s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to the high 60s by this morning as crude extended on the Saudi refinery strikes and the yen channel opened up, while the dominant mode moved from normal to mixed as cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The near-term focus is the 13:30 UTC US cash reopen after the Labor Day holiday, where concentrated post-holiday order flow lifts conditional tail into the low teens before easing through the midday lull and past the 15:00 UTC NY Fed inflation expectations print. Overnight, two channels can produce a step change in either direction: Middle East energy headlines, which carry simultaneous escalation and Hormuz de-escalation strands, and Tokyo-hours yen strength into the 17-18 September Bank of Japan meeting. Beyond this horizon, PPI on 10 September, Oracle results the same evening, CPI on 11 September and the 15-16 September FOMC meeting form the event stack; conditional tail is raised only modestly at the end of the horizon to reflect that build-up rather than any observed structure.
